title: Staged deployment failure hypothesis log and safety upgrades
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: After the 2026-02-02 staged rollout of semantic-sim-2.1 to hosted customers, we observed a regression that escaped canary checks and resulted in elevated hallucination rates and increased token error responses. This ticket collates hypotheses from the on-call and post-incident review, captures agreed runbook and safety changes, and tracks follow-ups required to reduce blast radius for future staged deployments.
incident_summary: Background: semantic-sim-2.1 was deployed with a 10% canary, 20% A/B shadow for metrics, and shadow traffic mirroring. Within ~30 minutes, we saw: (1) hallucination proxy metric (semantic-coherence-score) drop by 18% vs baseline, (2) token-level error rate increase from 0.03% to 0.9%, (3) p95 latency spike from 220ms to 1.2s for sequences >512 tokens. Canary alert rules did not trigger because our canary health rule combined signals and used sliding windows that diluted the short spike. Customer reported errors corresponded to the tail latency and token errors. Immediate action was manual rollback to v2.0 after 45 minutes.
hypothesis_log: H1: Model change introduced a rare failure mode for long-context generation (KV cache fragmentation) causing elevated latency and token errors for sequences >512 tokens.
H2: Metric aggregation window for canary health (5m median + 10m smoothing) masked a 15-45 minute burst; thresholds too permissive for token-error spikes.
H3: Shadow traffic and A/B instrumentation were not surfacing the coherence regression to the quality monitor because the coherence evaluator used sampling biased toward short queries.

H4: Automatic rollback circuit-breaker didn't execute because the p95 latency rule was tied to an absolute threshold that didn't account for dynamic baseline changes during traffic shifts (regional imbalance).
H5: Post-processing change in tokenizer mismatch between hosting runtime and offline eval introduced subtle off-by-one tokenization leading to hallucination in edge cases.
Notes: hypotheses originated from on-call logs, local reproductions, and initial kernel traces.
decision_log: 2026-02-03: Rollback decision validated by lead on-call (Marcus Li) after manual verification and customer impact review.
2026-02-10: Post-incident review agreed to tighten canary alert windows and add targeted probes for long-context request profiles.
2026-02-17: Approve prototype of a synthetic canary agent (SCA) that runs a representative long-context prompt suite every 2 minutes against canary subset.
2026-02-25: Agree to decouple token-error alerts from smoothed median by adding a burst detector on short windows (1m, 3m) and require auto-rollback on sustained breach.
2026-03-05: Decided to add a deterministic tokenizer validation step in rollout preflight to detect offline vs runtime token mismatch.
2026-03-09: Approved changes for rollout config: default canary to 5% for major model architecture changes; require minimum canary duration of 60 minutes with synthetic probes.
runbook_changes: Preflight: add tokenizer parity check (offline-vs-runtime) as blocking gate in release pipeline. Owner: infra-runtime (PR #4578).
Preflight: require a synthetic canary agent (SCA) config file with representative prompts for long-context (>512) and multimodal requests. Owner: eng/lifecycle - design spec in Confluence.
Monitoring: add short-window burst detectors for token-error-rate (1m, 3m) that trigger PagerDuty if token-error-rate > 0.25% sustained for 3 consecutive 1m windows.

Rollback: auto-rollback if any two of the following occur within 10 minutes: token-error-rate burst >0.25% (1m window), p95 latency > 3x baseline for >5 minutes, synthetic canary coherence score drop > 12%.
Post-rollback: automatic capture of full KV cache and kernel traces for last 60 minutes; persist to s3://redwood-incidents/ENG-24811/ for RCA.
actions: A1: Implement and deploy SCA prototype (small Go agent) and run against canary pool. Owner: Marcus Li. Due: 2026-03-12. GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/synthetic-canary/pull/12
A2: Change canary alert rules: add 1m/3m burst detectors and adjust smoothing parameters. Owner: Elena Rossi. Due: 2026-03-08. Config PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/monitoring/pull/243
A3: Add tokenizer parity preflight check into the CI pipeline (runtime-tokenizer vs offline-tokenizer). Owner: Soham Patel. Due: 2026-03-05. CI Job: ci/tokenizer-parity
A4: Instrument KV cache metrics per-request and expose fragmentation metric (kv-frag-ratio). Owner: Yun Park. Due: 2026-03-20.
A5: Update rollout defaults: reduce initial canary to 5% for model-major releases and require SCA run pass. Owner: Product Ops (Aisha Khan). Due: 2026-03-15.

A6: Add smoke suite for long-context prompts to our eval harness and include as mandatory smoke in the deployment pipeline. Owner: Research (Dr. Sofia Martinez). Due: 2026-03-10. Eval link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/long-context-smoke
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic canary agent deployed to canary hosts and synthetic coherence metric visible in console per-canary pool.
Burst detectors active in production and unit-tested in staging with synthetic breach scenarios.
Tokenizer parity preflight job exists and is green for PRs; releases blocked on parity failure.
Auto-rollback rule implemented in rollout controller and validated in a staging end-to-end test where injected token errors trigger rollback without human intervention.
Documentation updated: rollout runbook, preflight checklist, and postmortem summary published to Confluence.
Two downstream follow-ups assigned: KV cache metric instrumentation and rollout-config defaults change.
review_feedback: PM feedback (Aisha Khan): prefer conservative defaults for canary percentage and require SCA pass for all major/minor model upgrades.
Design feedback (Sofia Martinez): add visualization in Console for synthetic canary traces and allow drilling into the example prompts that failed.
Security feedback (Eva Goldberg): S3 incident artifacts must be encrypted and access-audited; integrate with customer-facing redaction pipeline for PII in traces.
On-call feedback (Devon O'Neil): make burst detector alerts page with mitigation checklist and automated rollback enable toggle for Site Reliability Engineers.
postmortem_learnings: Aggregation and smoothing are useful for noise reduction but dangerous when applied uniformly across orthogonal signals. Token-error bursts require short-window detectors.
Shadow traffic and A/B metrics are only as good as the evaluators used; sampling bias (favoring short queries) masked quality regressions for long-context flows.
Automated rollback needs clear, conservative multi-signal rules to avoid both false positives and delayed rollbacks; composition of signals should be tunable per-model.
Simulated/ synthetic canaries that exercise real long-tail behavior are an effective early-warning mechanism for regressions not seen in offline evals.
followups: F1: KV cache fragmentation investigation & mitigation plan (owner: Yun Park). Deliverable: kernel patch proposal. Due: 2026-04-01.
F2: Console integration for SCA traces and failure drill-down (owner: Sofia Martinez). Due: 2026-03-22.
F3: Runbook training for on-call teams: tabletop exercise simulating SCA failures and automated rollback. Owner: Devon O'Neil. Run date: 2026-03-25.
F4: Release note and customer communication template for staged rollout incidents (owner: Aisha Khan). Due: 2026-03-12.
